The AFX-operated cross-chain/USDC custody bridge on Arbitrum was exploited. The attacker used compromised validator hot keys to meet the quorum and drain approximately $24.15 million USDC. The funds were bridged to Ethereum and swapped for ETH. Arbitrum’s native bridge was unaffected, and AFX’s core trading infrastructure remained secure. The team suspended bridge operations and is investigating with security partners.

Five compromised validator signatures cleared the two-thirds threshold guarding a bridge, draining $24.15 million from AFX Trade's USDC custody bridge contract on Arbitrum and moving it out through the same public rails everyone else uses.

AFX Trade's AFX-operated custody bridge released 24,150,000 USDC on Arbitrum on 2026-07-22 after a multi-stage intrusion reached validator-related infrastructure and produced enough real signing authority to satisfy the bridge's withdrawal rules. AFX's 2026-07-25 disclosure describes a supply chain intrusion that began when a developer cloned a malicious repository after a Telegram contact, then spread through AFX's JFrog environment and internal systems until it reached validator-related infrastructure. The bridge accepted a withdrawal that carried sufficient real signing authority under its configured quorum rules. No public evidence in the consulted…
